chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Al-Halby, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said, 'There is no greeting (taslim) in the prayer upon the deceased.'

key_terms.تَسْلِيمٌ: Greeting (the ritual turning of the head to the right and left to conclude prayer)

ai.seo_question: Does the funeral prayer include the final greeting (taslim)?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes that the funeral prayer (Salat al-Mayyit) lacks the final salams (greetings), distinguishing it from the five daily prayers and highlighting its unique status as a supplication rather than a full ritual prayer. This ruling is significant in Shia jurisprudence for defining the boundaries of ritual acts (ibadat) and underscores the principle that specific details of worship must be derived from the Imams' teachings rather than analogy. The absence of taslim reflects the prayer's focus on intercession for the deceased, aligning with the broader theological view of the deceased's transition to the barzakh.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Abdullah Bin Muskan, from Al Halby who said,
‘Abu Abdullahasws said, ‘There is no greeting in the Salaat upon the deceased’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn Sinan from ’Abd Allah ibn Muskan from al-Halabiy who has said the following: “
Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘There is no Salam (the phrase of offering greeting of peace) to end Salah (prayer) for a deceased.’”
